headline: Winter Hill urinal and Somerville High tile repairs recommended to be marked complete; bathroom repairs and MSBA updates kept in committee.
summary: Commissioner Eric Weisman said gas-powered leaf blowers should not be used when children are outside at schools. The department is working to find replacement bathroom partitions at Winter Hill Innovation School, which has had repeated vandalism. The MSBA board voted to move the Winter Hill and Brown Schools project to schematic design.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 6, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Recommended to be marked work completed, a request that DPW use electric leaf blowers on school grounds during school hours.
Recommended to be marked work completed, a request to immediately repair the urinal at Winter Hill Innovation School.
Kept in committee a request to repair broken plumbing, appliances, and privacy treatments in Winter Hill Innovation School bathrooms.
Kept in committee a request for an update on when the school buildings maintenance project website will be available.
Recommended to be marked work completed, a request for updates on exterior tiles on the Somerville High School building.
Kept in committee a request for regular updates on the MSBA process for the Winter Hill and Brown Schools.

## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council School Building Facilities and Maintenance Committee Meeting Minutes

Tuesday, November 17, 2026

6:00 PM

Joint Meeting with the School Committee's School Building Facilities and Maintenance

Committee

- This meeting was held virtually via Zoom and was called to order at 6:01 pm
- by Chair Link and adjourned at 7:06 pm with a roll call vote of 3 in favor (Councilors Scott, Sait and

Link), none opposed, and none absent.

Others present: Leiran Biton - School Committee Member, Laura Pitone - School Committee Member, Elizabeth Eldridge - School Committee Member, Richard Raiche - Director of Infrastructure, Eric Weisman - Department of Public Works Commissioner, Danielle Barry - Facilities, Safety and Transportation Coordinator and Delaney Fisher-Cassiol - Clerk of Committees

The committee went into recess at 6:04 pm and returned at 6:05 pm on a roll call vote of 3 in favor (Councilors Scott, Sait and Link), none opposed, and none absent.

Roll Call

Present: Ward Two City Councilor Jefferson Thomas (J.T.) Scott, Ward Five City Councilor Naima Sait and City Councilor

- At Large Jon Link

1. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the School Building Facilities and Maintenance

Minutes

Committee Meeting of October 6, 2026.

(ID # 26-1519 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- Ward Two City Councilor Scott, Ward Five City Councilor
- Sait and City Councilor At Large Link

2. Resolution

By Councilor Link

(ID # 26-1499 ) That the Commissioner of Public Works, in consideration of children with

- sensory sensitivities, utilize electric leaf blowers when doing maintenance
- on school grounds during school hours.

Chair Link explained that his children attend the school and that parents had brought the issue to his attention. Department of Public Works

Commissioner Eric Weisman noted that gas-powered leaf blowers are being phased out and are no longer being purchased, although the department still

has some in its inventory. He explained that they are useful for moving wet leaves but reiterated that they should not be used when children are outside

- at schools. He has since reinforced this with his team.

- Commissioner Weisman expressed his willingness to continue the
- conversation online or offline, and Danielle Barry, Facilities, Safety and

Transportation Coordinator, concurred, noting that she is always available to collaborate with DPW.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED

3. Resolution

By Councilor Strezo

(ID # 26-1469 ) That the Commissioner of Public Works immediately repair the urinal

- fixture, otherwise known as 'The Blaster', at the Winter Hill Innovation

School and present written updated work timelines on a regular basis until the urinal fixture is entirely repaired.

Department of Public Works Commissioner Eric Weisman noted that the first-floor urinal has been repaired. School Committee Member Leiran Biton

added that the concern had been raised by a student during a public comment period, and School Committee Member Liz Eldridge clarified that

- the comment was made at the end of September.

Commissioner Weisman noted that, based on a review of 311 requests, repairs have been made to the urinal and other bathroom fixtures repeatedly, only for them to be damaged again. He added that the department had

replaced 10 bathroom door partitions at the school and eventually exhausted its supply, requiring the use of plywood, which was also subsequently

damaged. He emphasized that DPW works to stay on top of repairs and would appreciate support in keeping the bathrooms in functioning order.

- Laura Pitone noted that the school remains a concern, and Commissioner
- Weisman reiterated that it remains a priority for the department.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED

4. Resolution

By Councilor Strezo

(ID # 26-1468 ) That the Commissioner of Public Works repair all broken and inoperable

- plumbing, appliances and privacy treatments of the Winter Hill Innovation

School bathrooms and provide regular work timelines in writing, detailing when work will be initiated to when work is anticipated to be fully

- completed.

Department of Public Works Commissioner Eric Weisman noted that the department is working to source replacement bathroom partitions. He

explained that the parts are specific to the manufacturer and that the department aims to maintain a uniform appearance. He also noted that the bathrooms have experienced repeated vandalism. In response to a question

from Councilor Scott, Commissioner Weisman clarified that the doors are made of molded plastic.

- Danielle Barry, Facilities and Safety Manager for Somerville Public

Schools, expressed appreciation for DPW's efforts to keep the bathrooms safe and usable in the interim. She added that the school district is working with school administration to mitigate further damage to the facilities.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE

5. Order

By Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-0135 ) That the Director of Infrastructure and Asset Management update this

- Council on when the school buildings maintenance project website will be
- available.

- Director of Infrastructure, Richard Raiche, noted that significant work is

underway across the schools and that the department has been communicating with impacted schools at the school level to parents using

established communication channels. He explained that the intent of this order is to establish an additional communication channel and that it remains a priority. He noted that the effort is a multi-departmental project and that the Infrastructure Department is currently understaffed by five positions, leaving staff stretched thin and limiting their capacity to begin work on this initiative. Councilor Sait noted that the item was submitted last year and that she has heard from residents in Ward 5 that Somerville Public Schools has

been more communicative with parents this year. She expressed interest in having Councilors included in these communications about school projects, and Director Raiche agreed to look into the feasibility of doing so.

- School Committee Member Laura Pitone noted that separate, prior requests

had also been made regarding proactive communication about maintenance schedules. Director Raiche explained that work on this initiative has also

been underway and remains under contract, but a vacancy in the program manager position has slowed progress.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE

6. Order

By Councilor Davis

(ID # 26-1452 ) That the Director of Infrastructure and Asset Management present on

- continued concerns related to exterior tiles on the Somerville High School

building, and provide updates on measures to identify and mitigate those concerns.

Director of Infrastructure Richard Raiche noted that for the tiles along the windows, Sunrise, the envelope contractor responsible for installing them, developed a solution involving additional reinforcement where the tiles meet

- the windowsills. The solution includes custom-manufactured, color-matched

L-brackets. The mockups have been approved, and the brackets are now being manufactured. Director Raiche estimated that manufacturing would

take another one to two weeks, after which the department plans to complete the installation over winter break to minimize disruption to the school. In

- response to a question from School Committee Member Leiran Biton,

Director Raiche explained that most of the work can be completed from inside the building, allowing approximately 90 percent of the work to proceed regardless of weather conditions. However, some portions could be

delayed by weather if there were to be a big storm because they require the use of a boom lift.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED

7. Resolution

By Councilor Link and Councilor Mbah

(ID # 26-0241 ) That the Administration provide the Committee on School Building

- Facilities and Maintenance with regular updates on the Massachusetts
- School Building Authority (MSBA) process for the Winter Hill and Brown
- Schools.

- Director of Infrastructure, Richard Raiche, noted that the Massachusetts

School Building Authority (MSBA) Board voted to advance the project from the feasibility phase to schematic design. He explained that the consultant

team is committed to moving the project forward as quickly as possible and has begun work on multimodal transportation options for the school. He also

noted that a community forum was held the previous week and was well attended, with participants providing feedback on play structures and building colors. Chair Link noted the school's proximity to the Community

Path and expressed interest in the multimodal transportation options being developed.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE
